key_insight: A mean-flow adjoint built on the homogenized lattice Boltzmann method can provide practical sensitivity gradients for porous-cylinder flows from steady laminar to turbulent regimes while avoiding the memory burden of full transient checkpointing.
engineering_relevance: This enables more scalable shape and porosity optimization for flow control, drag reduction, and energy-dissipation design in unsteady and turbulent fluid systems.
method: Model porous cylinders with HLBM and Brinkman penalization to represent solid structures as local porous media.
Compute mean-flow adjoint sensitivities for drag and energy dissipation rather than full time-dependent adjoints.
Use automatic differentiation to generate adjoint kernels with SGS turbulence models for LES and compare against frozen turbulence assumptions.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a systematic study across steady laminar, unsteady, and turbulent cases, including a proof-of-concept at Re = 3900 with LES-based automatic differentiation.
watch_item: Mean-flow adjoint and SGS-generated kernels may still depend on modeling assumptions, so gradient accuracy and robustness should be checked carefully against turbulence closures and frozen-turbulence approximations.
paper_title: Mean-Flow Adjoint Sensitivity Analysis of Unsteady Flow Around Porous Cylinders Using a Homogenized Lattice Boltzmann Method
